evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We're rolling out door-to-door condom sales through 120 community health agents in two districts of Zambia, starting next month. The intervention as designed has three parts: a four-step household visit script (ask who's home, explain the product and the subsidized price, offer the pack, agree a restock date), a laminated price card the agent shows so the price is the same at every door, and a restock within seven days when an agent runs out. Agents fill in a paper sales log daily; twelve district coordinators supervise them. It's our own NGO staff, not government. The data are for learning and support only, we've said that to the agents. We can afford two monitors per district with motorbikes. What should the fidelity monitoring look like?
evals.expected_output: A fidelity monitoring plan in the output template that covers the script, the price card, and the restock, each with indicators, sources, thresholds, and owners.
assertions: Opens with a few plain sentences to the user, and marks each of the three parts essential or adaptable, saying what it changes for the person receiving it.
Gives adherence, dose, and quality as separate indicators.
Every essential part has at least one source other than the agents' own sales log, and household back-checks confirm that visits happened, not what the agent said.
Every threshold names an action and the role that takes it.
States that the data stay out of appraisal, pay, and discipline.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Our CHWs aren't following the protocol. Set up fidelity monitoring for us.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the program's parts, who delivers them, and what the data are for, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks what the protocol's parts are and who delivers each.
Asks how many CHWs there are and who supervises them.
Asks what the monitoring data will be used for.
Does not produce indicators or a plan.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: We support the district health office in a district of Rajasthan that runs monthly immunization camps with government ANMs (auxiliary nurse midwives). The camp design is: the ANM arrives by 9am, the ASHA worker has mobilized mothers the day before with a home visit, the vaccine cold box is checked on arrival, and every child gets a card entry. The district medical officer wants our monitoring data so he can dock the pay of ANMs who miss camps or arrive late. We don't have a data-sharing agreement with the district yet, just a verbal understanding. Can you design the monitoring plan?
evals.expected_output: The skill plans the parts and indicators it safely can, says the plan to dock pay and the missing agreement must be settled first, and names who to bring in.
assertions: Produces the essential-parts and indicator tables for the four parts of the camp design.
Says that using the data to dock pay conflicts with the plan's data-use rule and should be settled before launch.
Tells the user to involve an implementation researcher and the district's human-resources or administrative lead.
Says a written data-sharing agreement is needed before any observation, with the district's data-governance office or counsel.
Does not design feedback that feeds pay decisions.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Our savings-group reminder program in Butuan ended last year. Attendance at the group meetings was about 40% and the savings effect was basically zero. We have the facilitators' logs and the endline survey. Was it a bad idea or did we just deliver it badly?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the program is over and the question is whether the idea or its delivery failed, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the program is finished and the question looks back at what happened.
Does not produce a fidelity monitoring plan.
